answer: For a poll on a juniper garden and its vine sculpture, each ballot must include an original garden plan. A judge compares it with submitted plans and the published design requirements, accepting it only if it meets them and is not substantially similar; otherwise the ballot is rejected. An echo of an earlier plan fails. Extra votes require additional distinct plans, costing design effort. Judgment is subjective, and generative tools can lower the cost; this prices submissions, not identities.
